open.heading:
The date comes first,
{{not the problem.}}
body: Sunbeam places its parent–teacher meetings on the **academic calendar for the session**, alongside the examination dates, the terms and the holidays. The consequence is small and worth stating: a parent knows the date months before the meeting, and can read it against the examination it follows.

A meeting called at short notice has already said something before anyone speaks — that something has gone wrong. A meeting that was always in the calendar has not, which is what makes it possible to sit down about a child who is doing perfectly well.
The dates themselves are not published online. The [academic calendar](/academics/academic-calendar/) page sets out what the school says the calendar carries.

agenda.heading:
With a printed
{{agenda.}}
body: The forum is a panel session, and its agenda is projected in the room rather than kept at the front. That agenda is worth reading: **four of its twelve items** are the ones parents rarely get a formal channel for — *quality of classroom teaching, pace of teaching, quality of assignment,* and *correction of notebooks.*
The forum has its own page under [Parent Partnership](/academics/parent-partnership/parents-forum/); reports sit in the [parent portal]({resultsUrl}).

why.heading:
Four things,
{{and the reason for each}}
body: The cycle these meetings sit inside is on [Assessment & Support](/academics/assessment/).

cells.label: Scheduled early
cells.value: The date is placed on the session calendar before the year starts, so a family plans around it rather than reacting to it.

cells.label: Conversations that help
cells.value: A meeting that was always in the calendar carries no message of its own — which is what makes it possible to sit down about a child who is doing perfectly well.

cells.label: Aligned on progress
cells.value: Four of the twelve forum items are academic quality: classroom teaching, pace, assignments and the correction of notebooks.

cells.label: A record that stays
cells.value: Term reports and results sit in the parent portal between meetings, so the conversation has something to be read against.

close.heading:
Read it against
{{the calendar.}}
body: The school publishes that PTMs are on the session calendar and that reports sit in the parent portal. How many meetings a year, how long they run and whether they are by appointment are not published — and no photograph of a PTM exists on the school's site.
